whatItDoes: A phone-first bench page. You pick a PartForge FLIGHT declaration (one of the seven templates, or a pasted .scad) and type readings of the machined part, or GO/NO-GO results, against it. Each feature gets its own row, one per hole. A verdict needs a named instrument with a resolution. Each feature comes out IN, OUT, UNDECIDED or NOT MEASURED. Sizes are compared exactly as decimals in BigInt picometres, limits included, and every reading must be in, not just the mean. A 10:1 rule-of-thumb flag, a near-limit flag and an off-step flag are shown but never change a verdict. The part as a whole is INCOMPLETE until every row has a verdict and the operator and date are recorded. It is NONCONFORMING as soon as one row is OUT. Optionally, PartForge's measurement report (browser shape or `cli.mjs check` envelope) can be imported into a separate "as modelled" column that never fills a reading. A report for another part or another revision is refused. The record can be exported as JSON bound by the sha256 of the FLIGHT block, or as Markdown in the ICD's column order. A record from another revision is refused on resume.
testsPin:
ledger.test.mjs, 25 tests. It pins to these outside references:
- The FLIGHT-block sha256 of all 7 templates, computed by coreutils (`sed -n '/FLIGHT-BEGIN/,/FLIGHT-END/p' | sha256sum`), e.g. bulkhead ea41c20b0c1ba268….
- SHA-256 against the three FIPS 180-2 vectors and node:crypto on 400 strings.
- PartForge's own verbatim parseFlight/flightCounts: bulkhead 5 critical / 2 bores / 4 hole entries / 4 gauges / 2 loads, as the proposal said. Hole rows match the templates' MAKE lines ("10 holes", "8 holes", "mill 8 × 6.40").
- The GO/NO-GO pairs in the templates' own inspection plans against their declared limits: five bound their band, the fin's 4.38 GO does not.
- Report rows produced by PartForge's verbatim measurementRows() from an INVENTED flightRows object in the shape flightCheck() writes.
- With the checkout present: build-data --check is fresh, the ICD header string appears verbatim in index.html, and every template FLIGHT block appears verbatim in index.html.
- Hand-worked checks:
  - 6.6+0.1 = 6.699999999999999 in floating point, yet a 6.700 reading on the 6.60±0.10 hole is IN.
  - An oval OD read 146.14 and 146.26 is OUT, with mean 146.2000 and worst margin −0.010.
  - 5.7539 in is OUT by 0.00094 mm.
  - Inch limits are rounded inward: 5.75394/5.75787 and 0.49804/0.50196.
  - Bolt circle at 55·cos45 = 38.891.

findingsAboutSourceRepo:
PartForge at 0974a62. These are reported in the README and not fixed.

1. [Certain] tests/templates/fin.scad:38 (copied at index.html:2220) inspects the tab holes "with 4.38 GO / 4.60 NO-GO pins". fin.scad:30 declares them 4.50 ± 0.10, so the lower limit is 4.40. The GO pin is 0.02 mm under that limit: a hole between 4.38 and 4.40 passes the plan but fails the declaration. The other five GO/NO-GO pairs in the templates' plans sit exactly on their limits.
2. [Certain] tests/templates/bulkhead.scad:32 declares the "terminal block #8-32 tap drill" holes at 3.45 ± 0.10. Its own plan (:43) checks them "with a 2B thread plug gauge after tapping". After tapping, the 3.45 diameter no longer exists on the article, so it can only be verified in process. [Likely] The FLIGHT schema has no in-process dimension.
3. [Certain] tests/templates/av-sled.scad:24: neither check can show conformance to the declared band.
   - A 6.35 mm rod is used for holes declared 6.45 … 6.75, so it sits 0.10 mm below the lower limit.
   - A single 3.9 mm pin is used for holes declared 3.85 … 4.15, with nothing on the upper limit.
4. [Likely] mfgSheet() at index.html:6699-6702 puts the mesh's OK/FAIL in a column headed "Result" on the tier-A sheet, with no column for the article. A reader could take it as an inspection result; roadmap-evaluation.md:853 names the same risk.
5. [Certain] Neither measurementReport() (index.html:6816) nor the cli check envelope carries a FLIGHT-block hash. firstPartName() (:7166) returns 'part' for any file without a PART line, so binding a report to a revision is weak.
6. [Certain] Stale line numbers: roadmap-evaluation.md:659 cites index.html:3726 and :5634/5636. At 0974a62 these are :3964 and :6640/6642.

deviationsFromProposal:
1. The parser is PartForge's own: the DECL block from index.html:4646-4859 and measurementRows from headless/partforge.mjs:90-121, both copied verbatim by marker in build-data.mjs. The proposal planned a mirror parser.
2. The verdict requires every reading to be inside the band, not the mean. The proposal listed the mean first. A mean-based rule passes an oval part, and PartForge's cmmVerdicts (index.html:3849) also gates on the extremes.
3. Added a fourth verdict, UNDECIDED, and GO/NO-GO interval logic for size features (pins, plugs, rings). The templates' own inspection plans use pins, and a pair that does not sit on the limits cannot prove IN or OUT.
4. The 10:1 flag uses the larger of resolution and an optional stated accuracy, and I added near-limit and off-step flags. The 10:1 rule is labelled a rule of thumb, not a standard.
5. Hole position (pos_tol_mm) is not judged and is listed as not assessed. It needs a datum frame, and the evaluation's own objection about the radial offset still stands.
6. Completeness counts every row, gauges included, and also needs the operator and a valid date.
7. Added exact decimal arithmetic, inch entry, and inch limits rounded inward.
8. Snapshotted all seven templates, not four.
9. Quotations are given as they stand. The evaluation says "2-d caliper-entry subset" and "2-day provenance subset". The proposal's `cli.mjs check --asbuilt` does not exist, so it is listed as a landing change, not as a feature.
10. More than 50 readings, or a reading over 40 characters, is refused rather than truncated.
notBuilt:
- No real PartForge measurement report was imported. None exists in the checkout, and openscad-wasm is not installed here (headless/node_modules is absent). The "as modelled" import is tested only against an invented report, built through PartForge's own measurementRows().
- Hole position is not assessed, and neither are thread class, surface finish or form (flatness, roundness, taper).
- GO/NO-GO gauges are treated as exactly their nominal size. Gauge tolerance and wear are not modelled.
- There is no instrument calibration tracking and no guard banding (simple acceptance only).
- Only Chromium was used for testing. Touch was emulated in headless Chromium, no person has used the page at a bench, and Safari and Firefox are untested.
- The "tap drill" hint is a heuristic based on the feature name.
- Process note: my first scratch scripts were written to the shared scratchpad root as dbg.mjs and shots.mjs. If another builder had files with those names, I overwrote them. All my scratch has since been deleted.
- git status in the four repositories:
  - Partforge, asteroid-mining-planner, skyhook and Idea-Bank are all clean.
  - In Aster-Idea-Bank, my only change is the untracked ideas/19-caliper-ledger/.
